title: FSSAI issued 150 notices to major food brands in recent months over misleading ads

title: Being queer in Kashmir: Families, phones, friendships monitored, says report
description: A comprehensive report reveals the extensive control exerted over LGBTQIA+ individuals in Kashmir, highlighting issues such as monitored communications and scrutinized social interactions. The study emphasizes how family pressures and societal expectations surrounding marriage exacerbate marginalization. Additionally, educational institutions contribute to feelings of harassment and social exclusion. While some visibility fosters a degree of acceptance, it simultaneously increases the risk of backlash and surveillance for queer communities in the region.

title: Meta sued by former manager who claims he was fired over immigration letter
description: A former Meta manager filed a lawsuit alleging wrongful termination after objecting to an immigration letter. James Tillinghast claimed the letter overstated an employee's contributions and responsibilities. He also alleged Meta provided preferential immigration support to certain Chinese national employees. Tillinghast believes his dismissal was retaliation for raising these concerns. The lawsuit names Meta Platforms and a manager as defendants.

title: 1,200 Starlink satellites help map Earth's hard-to-observe upper atmosphere
description: Starlink satellites are now helping scientists map Earth's upper atmosphere. Researchers used orbital data from Starlink to estimate thermosphere density. This method creates a two-dimensional map of atmospheric density variations. The findings offer a new way to study this difficult-to-observe region. Commercial satellite data is becoming an unexpected scientific resource.

title: K'taka assembly passes apartment Bill: From ownership to redevelopment, rules defined
description: The Karnataka Assembly has passed a landmark bill to regulate apartment ownership and management effectively. This legislation lays the groundwork for Residents' Welfare Associations and offers guidance on managing common spaces. It also introduces a multi-tiered dispute resolution system. For redevelopment initiatives, a majority of 75% owner consent is now required, with owners who decline receiving double their property's assessed value.

title: ‘Crushed his lungs’: How a ‘minor’ dispute ended in Adobe techie's death
description: A software engineer was allegedly beaten to death by his wife's relatives following a dispute.  His family claims the attack was a pre-planned, calculated conspiracy to kill him.  The assault occurred at his home in Delhi after his wife summoned her family members.  Police have detained four individuals in connection with the brutal incident and are investigating.  The case is being registered under sections relating to murder and common intention.

title: Maine island bought by 27-year-old in 1964 later became wildlife sanctuary
description: Witch Island, previously inhabited by the infamous Anna Chittenden—referred to as the 'Witch of Wall Street'—has transformed into a wildlife sanctuary. After her brief stay, Jane Sewall took on the responsibility of safeguarding the isle from irresponsible tourists. In 1986, Sewall gifted the island to the Maine Audubon Society, which is now overseen by the Coastal Rivers Conservation Trust.

title: Medical debt relief model: MacKenzie Scott’s gifts erase $40 billion; $10 cancels $1,000
description: MacKenzie Scott pioneered large-scale medical debt relief through significant donations. Her gifts enabled the abolition of over forty billion dollars in medical debt. This initiative has provided relief to millions of families across all fifty states. Scott's model has also inspired other billionaires to contribute to debt eradication efforts. While philanthropic efforts offer immediate relief, systemic reforms are needed for lasting change.
